trust_boundaries.name: Inbound envelopes from the open agent network

remit_rules.excerpt: The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.

threats.summary: A sender that names itself user... is dispatched without any signature check, so the trust decision rests on an attacker-chosen four-character prefix rather than on key material.
A signed envelope observed once replays forever against a handler: expires and nonce are inside the signed digest but no ingress path checks either, and nonce is never populated on send.

Any agent on the network can drive a registered handler at will: dispatch consults only the schema digest and the user/agent address class, with no counterparty allowlist and no quota on the default path.
A malformed or unexpected payload cannot reach handler code, because dispatch is closed over registered schema digests and each payload is model-validated first.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction)
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.

threats.summary: GET /messages returns the entire cached message history to any caller who sets an X-Forwarded-For of 127.0.0.1, or to any web page the operator visits, because the loopback test reads a caller-supplied value and CORS is wildcarded.
The same reachable surface lets an unauthenticated caller re-register the agent in Agentverse against an endpoint of their choosing through POST /connect, or remove it through POST /disconnect.
The inspector is on unless the operator opts out, which both exempts /agent_info from the guard entirely and switches on in-memory retention of every message payload for a day.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent's own local key-value store.

threats.summary: Counterparty-supplied payloads are written verbatim into the agent's own store when message history is persisted and are read back into a later handler through ctx.session_history() with no provenance label or revalidation (checked: types.py:136-158 write path and types.py:188-201 read path — no filter, and storage/__init__.py:71-79 returns stored values as-is).

Quota accounting is keyed on the sender-supplied agent address and stored in the same key-value namespace as handler data, so a peer chooses the key its own rate-limit record is written under (checked: quota.py:252-274 — no namespacing or key validation).

trust_boundaries.name: Agent state file in the working directory

threats.summary: The key-value store is a plaintext JSON file written to the process working directory with default permissions, so any local user or mounted-volume reader sharing that directory can read persisted handler state and, when history storage is enabled, message payloads (checked: storage/__init__.py:94-96 — plain open() with no mode argument and no encryption; no chmod anywhere in the package).

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.

threats.summary: The Helm chart ships a working seed phrase as its default, and both the signing identity and the ledger wallet key are derived deterministically from that string, so anyone reading the repository holds the private keys of every unmodified deployment.

An agent created with a name and no seed writes its identity and wallet private keys as cleartext JSON to private_keys.json in the working directory with no permission restriction, and persists a different wallet key than the one it runs on.
Key material does not reach the public registry: the Almanac attestation is filtered to geolocation and the Agentverse profile carries only description, readme, avatar and banner.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds ... the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.

threats.summary: Every handler — including one processing an unverified inbound message — receives the agent's wallet and a ledger client able to broadcast transactions, and the framework offers no approval hook, threshold or audit point to hang a policy on (checked: agent.py:658-676 and context.py:280-282 — no gate in either module).

On a testnet registration that finds the wallet short of the fee, the runtime claims funds from a Fetch.ai faucet client built at import time — an outbound destination and a value-affecting action the operator never authorized.

trust_boundaries.name: Outbound sends, resolution and sync responses

remit_rules.excerpt: Outbound envelopes to other agents' resolved endpoints | Yes | No | Peer agents reached by address via the resolver.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions

threats.summary: A synchronous response carrying no signature at all skips verification and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply, and the core send helper never verifies a response envelope even when one is present.

Outbound traffic goes wherever the Almanac record says: endpoint URLs are taken from registry JSON with no scheme, host or allowlist check, so a forged or altered record redirects the agent's messages to a party of the attacker's choosing (checked: resolver.py:302-323 and context.py:489 — no validation between resolution and dispatch).
The agent cannot be impersonated on its own outbound path: every envelope built in Context.send_raw is signed with the agent identity before it is queued.

remit_rules.excerpt: Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.

threats.summary: A successfully handled message and a completed interval run leave no record at all, and what is written is free-form text with no session, sender or event-type field for anything downstream to parse.

No alert or halt primitive exists anywhere in the runtime, and the Almanac status update swallows every exception, so a failed deregistration or a run of verification failures is invisible even in the log.
The core send helper reports each message it sends to the Agentverse agents API by default, disclosing who the agent talks to and under which session with no operator opt-in.
Both published packages declare unbounded dependency floors, so a downstream install can silently cross a major version of uagents-core, cosmpy, ecdsa or requests that the project never tested.

The project's own build is reproducible — lockfiles are committed and CI installs with uv sync --locked — but nothing scans for known-vulnerable components and no SBOM is published, so exposure cannot be assessed when a CVE lands.
threats.remainder: no dependency, container or code scanning job and no SBOM anywhere in the repository, and the lock protects only the project's own test runs, never a downstream install

steps.summary: the inspector is registered by default, putting four REST endpoints on the agent's public socket
the caller sets X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 — or uses a web origin, since CORS is wildcarded — and the only guard passes
GET /messages returns the retained payloads of every message the agent has handled
POST /connect re-registers the agent in Agentverse against an endpoint the caller supplies
a sender claiming a user-prefixed address is admitted with no signature check
for signed traffic the check that does run never tests expires or nonce, so a captured envelope is equally good
handler selection consults no allowlist and no quota, so the message reaches the operator's handler
that handler holds an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval gate to clear
the chart's default seed is a working literal committed to the repository
the pod's UAGENT_SEED derives both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key deterministically
the reader of the repository can sign as that agent and move anything held under its derived address

notes.lane_fit: tools_mcp holds no LLM tools or MCP servers because the base runtime has none; it was populated with the framework's own declared capabilities (Almanac registration, address resolution) per the remit's Allowed Tools list, while the key-value store and envelope history stayed in agent_core as agent state. private_keys.json is a local file but sits in external_deploy under the lane table's secrets-store line.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences from the stored tags, all substantive rather than numbering-only: PRAX-2026-08-12-007 is stored ASI02 but the Agentic KB's compound table makes a missing approval gate on a consequential action LLM03 primary, with ASI02 reserved for a tool shown used wrongly — recorded here as LLM03. PRAX-2026-08-12-010 is stored ASI04, whose subject is runtime tool/agent composition and poisoned third-party sources; an unapproved automatic faucet call is an ungated consequential capability, so it is recorded as LLM03. PRAX-2026-08-12-013 is stored ASI08, but the spread test finds nothing propagating — a missing alert path is a pure observability gap, which both KBs route to RAISE with no OWASP code, so it is recorded as null. PRAX-2026-08-12-014 keeps its LLM04 primary and its ASI04 co-tag is dropped for the same runtime-composition reason. The stored-state and data-at-rest threats are left untagged rather than forced to LLM01/ASI06: the memory-poisoning codes presuppose a model consuming the store, and the base runtime holds no LLM. Edgeless nodes: quota-py-control (an opt-in protocol nothing wires in), values-yaml-deploy-surface (deployment posture evidence), pyproject-toml-deploy-surface (published-distribution and CI posture). Not modelled: the excluded uagents-adapter, uagents-ai-engine, examples/ and experimental/chat_agent trees, and the remaining src/uagents/experimental modules, which are not part of the default posture handed to a deployed agent; the uagents-core agentverse CLI, a read-only diagnostic that holds no credential and touches no agent state.
